target: È scesa dalla macchina.
english: She got out of the car.
tip: After essere the participle agrees with the subject: a woman è scesa (feminine), a man è sceso. Scendere gives sceso.

target: Andiamoci subito, è tardi!
english: Let's leave right away, it's late!
tip: Ci (there) attaches to the end of a let's-form: andiamo plus ci becomes andiamoci = let's go there.

target: Bevevo il latte ogni mattina.
english: I used to drink milk every morning.
tip: Bere keeps its older stem bev- in the imperfetto: bevevo = I used to drink.

target: Faceva molto caldo in agosto.
english: It used to be very hot in August.
tip: Weather uses fare: faceva caldo = it was hot, literally 'it made heat'. Also fare freddo for cold.

target: Sembra che loro non capiscano il problema.
english: It seems they don't understand the problem.
tip: Sembra che (it seems that) flips the following verb to the subjunctive: capiscano, not capiscono.

target: È corsa a casa appena ha saputo.
english: She ran home as soon as she found out.
tip: Verbs of motion take essere, and the participle shows who moved: È corsa means a woman ran, corso for a man.

target: Non aprire la porta a nessuno.
english: Don't open the door for anyone.
tip: Negative tu commands use non plus the infinitive: Non aprire, not the normal command form apri.

target: Passavamo le sere a giocare a carte.
english: We spent the evenings playing cards.
tip: The imperfetto describes an ongoing background: Passavamo le sere means 'we used to spend the evenings', a habit rather than a single event.

target: Ti riposi abbastanza?
english: Do you get enough rest?
tip: Riposarsi is reflexive: literally 'rest oneself', so Ti riposi keeps the ti where English just says 'you rest'.

target: Aveva paura del buio.
english: She was afraid of the dark.
tip: Italian uses avere, to have, for this feeling: aveva paura = was afraid, literally had fear.

target: Vorrei un caffè, per favore.
english: I would like a coffee, please.
tip: Vorrei is the conditional of volere and softens a request: vorrei un caffe = I would like a coffee.

target: Portava sempre gli occhiali da sole.
english: She always wore sunglasses.
tip: Sempre signals a past habit, so the verb goes imperfetto: portava sempre means 'she always wore'.

target: Ve lo ripeto un'altra volta.
english: I'm telling you again.
tip: When two pronouns stack, indirect comes before direct: ve lo means 'it to you', both sitting before ripeto.

target: Preferivo restare a casa il sabato.
english: I preferred to stay home on Saturdays.
tip: English 'I preferred' is simple past, but an ongoing preference needs the imperfetto in Italian: preferivo.

target: Quando è arrivata la polizia, il ladro scappava.
english: When the police arrived, the thief was fleeing.
tip: Passato prossimo (è arrivata) for event + imperfetto (scappava) for ongoing action.

target: Ci chiamiamo spesso.
english: We call each other often.
tip: Plural reflexive pronouns can mean each other, not just oneself: ci chiamiamo means we call each other.

target: Non scrivere sul muro!
english: Don't write on the wall!
tip: Negative commands to one person (tu) use non plus the infinitive: non scrivere means don't write.

target: Mi sveglio e faccio colazione.
english: I wake up and have breakfast.
tip: Reflexive verbs use reflexive pronouns (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si) before the conjugated verb: "Mi sveglio" (I wake up).

target: Abita da solo da tre anni.
english: He's been living alone for three years.
tip: Present tense plus da expresses duration: Abita da tre anni means 'he has been living for three years', still ongoing.

target: Quando siamo usciti, faceva già buio.
english: When we went out, it was already dark.
tip: Passato prossimo (siamo usciti) for event + imperfetto (faceva) for weather.

target: Da voi fa freddo in inverno?
english: Is it cold where you are in winter?
tip: Weather uses fare, not essere: fa freddo means it is cold, literally it makes cold.

target: Voglio che i bambini mangino la verdura.
english: I want the children to eat vegetables.
tip: "Volere che" + congiuntivo: expressing a wish about someone else's action. The subjunctive is mandatory.

target: Bisogna che io faccia una telefonata urgente.
english: I must make an urgent phone call.
tip: Bisogna che (it's necessary that) forces the subjunctive: io faccia, not faccio.

target: Quando l'ho incontrata, portava un vestito rosso.
english: When I met her, she was wearing a red dress.
tip: Passato prossimo (l'ho incontrata) for event + imperfetto (portava) for description.

target: Sembra che il tempo cambi ogni cinque minuti.
english: It seems the weather changes every five minutes.
tip: Sembra che (it seems that) triggers the subjunctive on the next verb: cambi, not cambia.

target: Bisogna che il ristorante migliori il servizio ai tavoli.
english: The restaurant must improve its table service.
tip: Bisogna che states a real need, but the action stays hypothetical, so it takes the subjunctive: migliori, not migliora.

target: Deve lavarsi le mani.
english: He needs to wash his hands.
tip: With an infinitive, the reflexive si attaches to the end: lavarsi means 'to wash oneself'.

target: Lui studiava mentre io dormivo.
english: He studied while I slept.
tip: Italian usually drops subject pronouns; Lui and io appear only for contrast: Lui studiava means HE studied, while I slept.

target: Si lava le mani prima di mangiare.
english: He washes his hands before eating.
tip: With reflexive verbs and body parts, Italian uses the article, not a possessive: si lava le mani = washes his hands.

target: Ho comprato un libro per mia madre.
english: I bought a book for my mother.
tip: Singular family members drop the article after a possessive: mia madre, not la mia madre.
